step1_figure.description: The netlist implements a modified version of the common-source amplifier in Fig 21.21. While the figure shows a simple CS amplifier with a current source load, the netlist uses a telescopic cascode topology (cascode NMOS and cascode PMOS load) to achieve the higher 'open circuit gain' discussed on page 673. It retains the exact AC coupling (100k Rs, 1uF Cbig) and DC self-biasing feedback (1G Rbig) shown in Fig 21.21.

cascode_output_resistance.description: The small-signal resistance looking into the drain of the cascode topology.

equation.formula: R_o \approx (1 + g_m R) r_o \approx g_m r_o^2
equation.explanation: The output resistance is boosted by the intrinsic gain (gm*ro) of the cascode device.
equation.assumptions: Assumes R = r_o (cascoded MOSFET topology) and neglects body effect.

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming a typical bias current I_D = 20uA and W/L = 10 for NMOS. g_m = sqrt(2 * un*Cox * (W/L) * I_D) = sqrt(2 * 270u * 10 * 20u) = 328 uS. r_o = 1 / (lambda * I_D) = 1 / (0.1 * 20u) = 500 kOhm. R_o_nmos = g_m * r_o^2 = 328u * (500k)^2 = 82 MOhm. For PMOS (W/L=20), g_m = sqrt(2 * 50u * 20 * 20u) = 200 uS. R_o_pmos = 200u * (500k)^2 = 50 MOhm. Total R_out = 82M || 50M = 31 MOhm.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends heavily on the exact parameterized W/L ratios and the resulting bias current from the SUB_1 bias network.

open_circuit_gain.description: The maximum possible gain attainable with a single MOSFET (or the intrinsic gain of the stage).

equation.explanation: The gain when the load is purely the transistor's own output resistance.
equation.assumptions: Assumes ideal current source load with infinite resistance.

sky130_expected.calculation: Using the previously calculated values: g_m1 = 328 uS, r_o1 = 500 kOhm. Intrinsic gain = -328uS * 500kOhm = -164 V/V. For the full cascode circuit, the gain is -g_m1 * R_out = -328uS * 31MOhm = -10,168 V/V (approx 80 dB).
sky130_expected.reasoning: The cascode topology significantly boosts the gain from the single-stage open circuit gain to roughly (g_m*r_o)^2 / 2.

slew_rate.description: The maximum rate at which the load capacitor can be charged or discharged.

equation.explanation: Limited by the maximum current the amplifier can source or sink into the load capacitance.
equation.assumptions: Assumes the amplifier is fully slewing (one side of the differential pair or current source is fully steering the tail current).

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming the bias circuit sets a maximum current of 20 uA (as in Ex 21.5). The netlist specifies Cload = 1e-13 F (0.1 pF). Slew rate = 20uA / 0.1pF = 200,000,000 V/s = 200 V/us.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Directly proportional to the bias current set by SUB_1 and inversely proportional to the fixed 0.1pF load.

input_capacitance.description: The effective capacitance looking into the input of the amplifier, dominated by the Miller effect.

equation.explanation: The gate-drain capacitance is multiplied by the voltage gain due to the Miller effect.
equation.assumptions: Assumes the gain A_v is large and constant up to the input pole frequency.

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming C_gs1 ~ 5 fF and C_gd1 ~ 1 fF for a small device. With a cascode gain |A_v| ~ 10,000, C_in = 5fF + 1fF*(1 + 10000) = 10.005 pF.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The extremely high gain of the cascode stage creates a massive Miller capacitance, even for small intrinsic C_gd.

input_pole.description: The frequency of the pole associated with the input node.

equation.explanation: Formed by the source resistance and the total input capacitance (including Miller capacitance).
equation.assumptions: Assumes a dominant Miller effect and a purely resistive source.

sky130_expected.calculation: Using R_s = 100 kOhm (from netlist) and calculated C_in = 10 pF. f_in = 1 / (2 * pi * 100k * 10p) = 159 kHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The large 100k source resistor combined with the massive Miller capacitance pushes this pole to a relatively low frequency.

output_pole.description: The frequency of the pole associated with the output node.

equation.explanation: Formed by the output resistance and the total output capacitance.
equation.assumptions: The text notes this equation can be inaccurate due to pole splitting when A_v decreases at high frequencies.

sky130_expected.calculation: Using R_out = 31 MOhm and C_out ~ C_load = 0.1 pF. f_out = 1 / (2 * pi * 31M * 0.1p) = 51.3 kHz. (Note: Pole splitting will likely push the actual output pole to a much higher frequency, as discussed on page 676).
sky130_expected.reasoning: The extremely high output resistance of the cascode makes the un-split output pole very low, potentially making it the dominant pole depending on the exact Miller capacitance.

transfer_function_zero.description: The frequency of the right-half-plane zero caused by feedforward through Cgd.

equation.explanation: Occurs because Cgd provides a feedforward path that bypasses the transconductance stage at high frequencies.
equation.assumptions: Assumes Cgd is the primary feedforward path.

sky130_expected.calculation: Using g_m1 = 328 uS and C_gd1 = 1 fF. f_z = 328u / (2 * pi * 1f) = 52.2 GHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Typically at a very high frequency in modern deep-submicron processes due to small parasitic capacitances and high gm.

step3_testbench.description: Measures the DC operating point, AC open-loop gain, bandwidth, and transient slew rate of the cascode amplifier.
